Both captures are real: two strongSwan 6.1.0 peers (R1, R3) negotiating IKEv2 through a transit router (R2) in Linux network namespaces, recorded with dumpcap on R2's interface r2-g1 and decoded with tshark 4.2.2. Frame sizes include the 14-byte Ethernet header. ESP runs UDP-encapsulated on port 4500 because the lab used strongSwan's userspace IPsec. The keys are throwaway lab keys, published on purpose; with them loaded, IKE_INTERMEDIATE is decoded with the IKE_SA_INIT key set and later messages with the re-derived set. Wireshark 4.2 shows exchange types 43 and 44 as "Unknown" and ML-KEM-768 as "Unknown (36)". Packets move one at a time here; in the capture, the two fragments of each ML-KEM message left R1 less than 0.3 ms apart. The packet tree, bytes, colours and packet list were checked line by line against tshark and the raw capture.
